answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity climb a spiral staircase, not a flat field. Each newcomer waits on a narrow ledge, a quarantined role with rewards, and rises one spiral turn at a time only through witnessed work. Every step sends a ripple outward: neighbours must co-sign the proof, and a ripple that reaches no independent witness dies. Two identities climbing the same spiral leave identical ripples, so overlapping ripples expose the pair and both are dissolved with their stakes slashed. Climbing is slow, copying is costly, and only contributors leave the ledge.
